chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who started with al-Marwah before al-Safa. He said, 'He must repeat (the ritual). Do you not see that if he started with his left hand before his right hand during wudu (ablution), he intended to repeat the wudu?'

key_terms.الصَّفَا: Al-Safa (the first hill in the Hajr area of Mecca)
key_terms.الْمَرْوَةِ: Al-Marwah (the second hill in the Hajr area of Mecca)
key_terms.يُعِيدُ: He repeats (referring to the ritual action)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim walks between Marwah and Safa in the wrong order?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the ruling for the Sa'i ritual, establishing that starting with Marwah before Safa is a defect requiring repetition. He employs a nuanced analogy from ablution (wudu), where beginning with the left hand signals an intent to restart, thereby illustrating how the pilgrim's deviation from the prescribed order invalidates the sequence. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the strict adherence to the Sunnah of the Prophet and the Imams in the structural integrity of Hajj rituals.
